questions.explain: „Today all books are five euros.“

questions.text: Yarınki açılış saatini söyleyen cümleyi duyduğun gibi yaz.
questions.explain: „Tomorrow we open at ten.“ — zaman ifadesi cümle başında da durabilir.

questions.text: What opens on Saturday?
options: a new shop for books and gifts
a new room about old maps
a bigger cloakroom by the door
questions.explain: „The new room about old maps opens on Saturday.“

title: I Am Late
intro: Arkadaşın seni bekliyor ama geciktin; önce iki cümle kur, sonra ona kısa bir mesaj yaz.

tasks.answer: Today I am twenty minutes late.
alternatives: I am twenty minutes late today.
tasks.hint: „be“ + süre + late kalıbı yeter; zaman ifadesi başta da sonda da durabilir.

tasks.tr: Lütfen benim için bir çay ısmarla.
tasks.answer: Please order a tea for me.
alternatives: Order a tea for me, please.
tasks.hint: Emir cümlesi özne almaz; kime yapıldığını „for me“ ile ya da doğrudan „me“ ile söylersin.

tasks.prompt: Arkadaşın seni bekliyor ama geciktin. Ona mesaj yaz: geç kaldığını söyle, nedenini yaz, ne kadar geç kalacağını belirt, o sırada ne yapmasını istediğini söyle ve özür dile.
checklist: Geç kaldığını ve nedenini yaz
Ne kadar geç kalacağını söyle
Beklerken ne yapmasını istediğini yaz
Özür dile ve vedalaş

phrases.de: I am sorry, I am late.

tasks.sample: Hi Bea, I am so sorry! The bus is not here and I am twenty minutes late. There is a problem on my line. Please do not wait outside, it is very cold. Go in and take our table by the window. Please order a tea for me. See you very soon!

title: w and v
intro: İngilizcede „w“ dudaklarla, „v“ ise diş ve dudakla çıkar; Türkçedeki tek v sesi ikisinin arasında kalır.

tasks.hint: „we“ ve „want“ yuvarlak dudakla, dişe değmeden; „visit“ ve „Vienna“ üst dişler alt dudakta.

confusions.fix: „w“de dişler dudağa değmez, „v“de değer; ikisini karıştırma.

tasks.hint: „van“ ve „very“ ikisi de v: üst dişler alt dudağa hafifçe dokunur.

confusions.fix: Dudakları yuvarlama; dişini dudağına koy ve titreştir: van, very.

tasks.hint: „where“ ve „wallet“ w ile başlar: dudaklar önce yuvarlak, sonra açılır.

confusions.fix: Ağzını „u“ der gibi yuvarla ve sonra kelimeye geç: uue-a, uo-lit.

tasks.hint: Aynı cümlede üç ses: „Vera“ v, „works“ ve „weekend“ w, „every“ yine v.

confusions.fix: Baştaki ada dikkat: Vera dişle, works dudakla.

tasks.hint: „have“ ve „five“ v sesi; „we“, „white“ ve „windows“ w sesi.

confusions.fix: „have“ ve „five“ dişli, „windows“ dudaklı: hev, fayv, uindouz.

tasks.hint: „give“ v ile, „water“ w ile başlar; iki kelime arka arkaya geliyor.

confusions.fix: İlkinde diş, ikincisinde dudak: giv, uo-ta.

tasks.hint: Üç kez v: Victor, lives, village. Cümlenin tamamı diş-dudak çalışması.

confusions.fix: Üçünde de üst dişler alt dudağa değsin; hiçbirinde dudak yuvarlanmaz.

title: I work or I am working?
intro: Türkçedeki tek „-yor“ eki İngilizcede ikiye ayrılır: alışkanlık başka biçim, şu an başka biçim ister.
focus: Present continuous ile present simple farkı

explanation.heading: İki ayrı iş
explanation.tr: Türkçede „çalışıyorum“ hem alışkanlığı hem şu anı anlatır. İngilizcede ikisi ayrılır: alışkanlık ve genel doğru için present simple (I work), tam şu an olan için present continuous (I am working).

examples.de: I work in a hospital.
I am working now.
It rains a lot in November.

explanation.heading: Biçim ve yazım
explanation.tr: Continuous iki parçadır: be + fiil-ing. Yazımda üç kural: sondaki sessiz e düşer (make → making), kısa ünlüden sonra son sessiz iki olur (sit → sitting), -y düşmez (study → studying).

examples.de: She is making tea.
They are sitting outside.
He is studying English.

explanation.heading: Bazı fiiller -ing almaz
explanation.tr: Durum bildiren fiiller continuous biçimde kullanılmaz: like, love, know, want, need, understand ve sahiplik anlamındaki have. „I am wanting“ yanlıştır, „I want“ doğrudur.

examples.de: I like this song.
She has two brothers.
We need help.

questions.text: Look! The baby ___.
questions.explain: „Look!“ tam şu anı gösterir, bu yüzden continuous gelir.

questions.text: She ___ to work by bus every day.
questions.explain: „every day“ alışkanlık bildirir: present simple ve üçüncü tekilde -es.

questions.text: I ___ this song very much.
questions.explain: „like“ durum fiilidir ve -ing biçimi almaz.

questions.text: We usually ___ (have) dinner at seven.
questions.explain: „usually“ alışkanlık bildirir ve „we“ ile fiil yalın kalır.

questions.text: Be quiet! I ___ (work).
questions.explain: Tam şu an olan bir iş: am + working.

questions.text: He ___ (not / watch) TV at the moment.
questions.explain: „at the moment“ continuous ister; olumsuz „not“ be ile fiil arasına girer.

questions.text: My parents ___ (live) in Bursa.
questions.explain: Sürekli bir durum, alışkanlık gibi anlatılır: present simple, çoğul özne.

questions.text: Soruyu doğru sıraya diz.
questions.explain: Soru kelimesi + be + özne + fiil-ing: What are you doing now?

questions.text: „I am wanting a coffee.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: „want“ durum fiilidir; doğrusu „I want a coffee.“

questions.text: „It is raining now.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: „now“ tam şu anı gösteriyor ve biçim be + -ing; cümle doğru.

title: The Old Cinema Opens Again
intro: Kasabanın eski sinemasının yeniden açıldığını duyuran kısa bir haber okuyacaksın.
text:
THE OLD CINEMA OPENS AGAIN

Good news for our town. The old cinema in Park Street opens again on the twelfth of March, after four years.

The building is the same, but inside everything is new: new seats, a new floor and a small café.

Tickets are seven euros. For children and students they are four euros. On Mondays all tickets are five euros.

The first film is a comedy from nineteen fifty-four. It starts at eight in the evening. Coffee and cake are free on the first day.

The cinema is open every day from four to eleven.

questions.text: What is the news?
options: A new cinema is very expensive.
questions.explain: Başlık ve ilk cümle aynı şeyi söylüyor: dört yıl sonra yeniden açılıyor.

questions.text: How much is a ticket for a student?
questions.explain: „For children and students they are four euros.“ Yedi euro normal fiyat, beş euro pazartesi fiyatı.

questions.text: Tickets are cheaper on Mondays than on other days.
questions.explain: „Tickets are seven euros … On Mondays all tickets are five euros.“

questions.text: The cinema opens on the ___ of March.
questions.explain: „… opens again on the twelfth of March, after four years.“

questions.text: What is free on the first day?
questions.explain: „Coffee and cake are free on the first day.“

questions.text: When is the cinema open?
options: only in the evening at eight
every day from four to eleven
questions.explain: „The cinema is open every day from four to eleven.“ Saat sekiz ilk filmin saati.

title: Two Pizzas, Please
intro: Telefonla yemek siparişi veren birini dinleyeceksin: ne istiyor, ne kadar tutuyor, ne zaman geliyor.

segments.speaker: Shop
segments.text: Bella Pizza, good evening.

segments.speaker: Kaan
segments.text: Good evening. I would like to order two pizzas, please.

segments.speaker: Shop
segments.text: Of course. Which ones?

segments.speaker: Kaan
segments.text: One with cheese and tomato, and one with mushrooms. Both big, please.

segments.speaker: Shop
segments.text: Big cheese and tomato, big mushroom. Anything to drink?

segments.speaker: Kaan
segments.text: Yes, two bottles of water. How much is it?

segments.speaker: Shop
segments.text: That is twenty-six euros fifty. What is your address?

segments.speaker: Kaan
segments.text: Rose Street fourteen, second floor. The name is Kaan.

segments.speaker: Shop
segments.text: Thank you. It comes in forty minutes. Please have the money ready.

segments.speaker: Kaan
segments.text: Great, thank you. Goodbye!

questions.text: What does Kaan order?
questions.explain: „… two pizzas, please“ ve sonra „two bottles of water“.

questions.text: How much is it?
questions.explain: „That is twenty-six euros fifty.“

questions.text: Kaan orders one small pizza.
questions.explain: „Both big, please.“ — ikisi de büyük.

questions.text: When does the food come?
questions.explain: „It comes in forty minutes.“

questions.text: Dükkânın son ricasını duyduğun gibi yaz.
questions.explain: „Please have the money ready.“ — emir cümlesi özne almaz.

questions.text: What is on the second pizza?
questions.explain: „One with cheese and tomato, and one with mushrooms.“

title: Winter Boots for Sale
intro: Dolabını boşaltıyorsun; önce iki cümle kur, sonra bir eşyanı satmak için küçük bir ilan yaz.

tasks.tr: Botlar bir yaşında ve çok sıcak tutuyor.
tasks.answer: The boots are one year old and very warm.
alternatives: The boots are very warm and one year old.
tasks.hint: Yaş için „be … year(s) old“ kalıbı kullanılır; sıfatlar „and“ ile bağlanır.

tasks.answer: You can pick them up on Saturday.
alternatives: On Saturday you can pick them up.
tasks.hint: „pick up“ ayrılabilir bir fiildir; zamir kullanılırsa mutlaka araya girer: pick them up.

tasks.prompt: Bir eşyanı satmak için küçük ilan yaz: ne satıyorsun, nasıl görünüyor, kaç yaşında ve ne durumda, fiyatı ne, alıcı onu ne zaman ve nereden alabilir.
checklist: Ne sattığını ve nasıl göründüğünü yaz
Yaşını ve durumunu söyle
Fiyatı yaz
Alma zamanını, yerini ve iletişimi yaz

phrases.de: You can pick it up on …

tasks.sample: For sale: winter boots, size thirty-eight, and a black coat, size M. The boots are brown and one year old, the coat is two years old. Both are warm and clean. The boots are twenty euros, the coat is thirty euros. Together forty-five. You can pick them up on Saturday between ten and six. I live in Rose Street fourteen. Please write me a message!

title: bad or bed?
intro: Türkçede tek bir e sesi var; İngilizcede ise açık „a“ ile kapalı „e“ iki ayrı sestir ve kelimeyi değiştirir.

tasks.hint: „bag“ ve „bad“ geniş bir sesle: ağzını aç, dilini indir — a ile e arası.

confusions.fix: Ağzını daha çok aç; kapalı e söylersen „beg“ ve „bed“ olur.

tasks.hint: „send“, „ten“ ve „letters“ üçünde de kapalı e: ağız daha kapalı, ses kısa.

confusions.fix: Burada geniş a yok; ağzını fazla açma: send, ten.

tasks.hint: „sat“ geniş, „bed“ kapalı. İki ses aynı cümlede yan yana.

confusions.fix: „sat“ açık ağızla, „bed“ kapalı ağızla; ikisini takas etme.

tasks.hint: „hand“ geniş a, „red“ kapalı e. Sondaki d ikisinde de duyulur.

confusions.fix: İlkinde ağzı aç, ikincisinde kapat: hand, red.

tasks.hint: „can“ ve „catch“ geniş; „pen“ kapalı.

confusions.fix: İlk iki kelimede ağız açık, sondaki „pen“de kapalı.

tasks.de: The man is at the desk.
tasks.hint: „man“ ve „at“ geniş; „desk“ kapalı e.

heard: The men is at the dask
confusions.fix: „man“ tekil ve geniş sesli; „men“ çoğul ve kapalı sesli.

tasks.hint: „Sally“, „has“ ve „cats“ geniş; „seven“ kapalı.

confusions.fix: Üç kelimede ağzını aç, yalnız „seven“de kapat.

title: can, can't and orders
intro: Yetenek ve izin için tek bir kelime yeter; rica ve emirde ise fiil hiç değişmez.
focus: can / can't ve emir kipi

explanation.heading: can hiç değişmez
explanation.tr: Türkçede yetenek fiile ek olarak girer: yüz-ebil-irim. İngilizcede ayrı bir kelime gelir: can. Bu kelime hiçbir kişide değişmez — üçüncü tekilde bile -s almaz — ve arkasından gelen fiil yalın kalır.

examples.de: I can swim.
She can swim very well.
He can play the guitar.

explanation.heading: Olumsuz, soru ve rica
explanation.tr: Olumsuzda „cannot“ ya da kısa biçim „can't“ kullanılır. Soruda „can“ başa geçer: Can you …? Aynı yapı hem yeteneği hem izni hem de kibar ricayı anlatır.

examples.de: I can't drive a car.
Can I sit here?
Can you open the window, please?

explanation.heading: Emir kipi: yalın fiil
explanation.tr: Emir ve yönergede özne yazılmaz ve fiil yalın hâliyle başta durur: Come in. Olumsuz için başa „Don't“ gelir: Don't be late. Nazikleştirmek için „please“ eklenir.

examples.de: Come in and sit down.
Don't forget your ticket.
Please close the door.

questions.text: She ___ swim very well.
questions.explain: „can“ üçüncü tekilde de değişmez ve arkasından yalın fiil gelir.

questions.text: ___ you open the window, please?
questions.explain: Rica „Can you …?“ ile kurulur; ayrı bir yardımcı fiil gerekmez.

questions.text: ___ late!
questions.explain: Olumsuz emir „Don't“ ile başlar ve arkasından yalın fiil gelir.

questions.text: I ___ (not / drive) a car.
questions.explain: Olumsuz biçim can't ya da cannot; asıl fiil yalın kalır.

questions.text: ___ (come) in and sit down.
questions.explain: Emir kipinde özne yazılmaz ve fiil yalın hâliyle başta durur.

questions.text: My brother ___ play the guitar very well.
questions.explain: Yetenek anlatılıyor ve „can“ hiçbir kişide değişmez.

questions.text: ___ (not / forget) your ticket!
questions.explain: Uyarı bir olumsuz emirdir: Don't + yalın fiil.

questions.text: Soruyu doğru sıraya diz.
questions.explain: Soruda „can“ başa geçer, sonra özne ve yalın fiil gelir: Can you help me, please?

questions.text: „He cans speak Italian.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: „can“ -s almaz; doğrusu „He can speak Italian.“

questions.text: „Please close the door.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: Emir kipinde özne yoktur ve fiil yalındır; „please“ cümleyi nazikleştirir.

title: Dog Walker Wanted
intro: Apartman girişindeki küçük iş ilanını okuyacaksın: kim aranıyor, ne zaman, ne kadar ödeniyor.
text:
DOG WALKER WANTED

Hello neighbors! I need help with my dog, Milo.

Milo is a small brown dog. He is six years old and very friendly. He is not good with cats, but he loves children.

I work from Monday to Friday, from nine to five. I need somebody for one walk every day, at about one o'clock. The walk is thirty or forty minutes in the park.

I pay ten euros for one walk.

You can start in March. You do not need a car; I live in Lime Street eight, near the bus stop.

Please call me: 0176 22 88 41. Ask for Marta.

questions.text: What does Marta need?
options: a driver who takes Milo to the park
a place for Milo from Monday to Friday
somebody for one walk a day
questions.explain: „I need somebody for one walk every day, at about one o'clock.“

questions.text: When is the walk?
questions.explain: Dokuzdan beşe Marta'nın çalışma saatleri; yürüyüş „at about one o'clock“.

questions.text: Milo is good with cats.
questions.explain: „He is not good with cats, but he loves children.“

questions.text: Marta pays ___ euros for one walk.
questions.explain: „I pay ten euros for one walk.“

questions.text: How old is Milo?
questions.explain: „He is six years old and very friendly.“

questions.text: What do you not need for this job?
questions.explain: „You do not need a car; I live in Lime Street eight, near the bus stop.“

title: Welcome on the City Bus Tour
intro: Şehir turunda rehberin karşılama konuşmasını dinleyeceksin: tur ne kadar sürüyor, nerede duruluyor, kurallar neler.

segments.text: Hello everyone and welcome! My name is Rick and I am your guide today.
The tour is ninety minutes. We stop two times: at the castle and at the river.
At the castle you have twenty minutes. Please come back to the bus at half past three.
The bus is warm, so you can leave your coats here. Nobody comes in.
Please do not eat on the bus, but water is fine.
If you have a question, come to the front. I am here all the time.
And now, look on your right: that is the old market. Let's go!

questions.text: Who is Rick?
questions.explain: „My name is Rick and I am your guide today.“

questions.text: How long is the tour?
questions.explain: „The tour is ninety minutes.“ Yirmi dakika kaledeki mola.

questions.text: The bus stops two times during the tour.
questions.explain: „We stop two times: at the castle and at the river.“

questions.text: When must people come back to the bus?
questions.explain: „Please come back to the bus at half past three.“

questions.text: Turun süresini söyleyen cümleyi duyduğun gibi yaz.
questions.explain: „The tour is ninety minutes.“ — süre için „be“ yeter.

questions.text: What is on the right at the start?
questions.explain: „… look on your right: that is the old market.“

title: My Hotel Review
intro: Kaldığın bir yeri internette değerlendireceksin; önce iki cümle kur, sonra kısa bir yorum yaz.

tasks.answer: In the morning the room is very quiet.
alternatives: The room is very quiet in the morning.
tasks.hint: Günün bölümü „in the“ ile söylenir ve cümlenin başında da sonunda da durabilir.

tasks.answer: Breakfast starts at seven in the morning.
alternatives: In the morning, breakfast starts at seven.
tasks.hint: Saat için „at“, günün bölümü için „in the“ kullanılır.

tasks.prompt: Kaldığın bir oteli ya da pansiyonu internette değerlendir: nerede, neyi beğendin, kahvaltı nasıl, iyi olmayan bir şey ve kaç yıldız veriyorsun.
checklist: Yerini ve nasıl gidildiğini yaz
Odayı ve kahvaltıyı anlat
İyi olmayan bir şeyi söyle
Kaç yıldız verdiğini yaz

phrases.de: Only one thing is not good: …

tasks.sample: Hotel Rosa is in the old town, five minutes from the station. The room is small but very clean, and the bed is good. Breakfast starts at seven in the morning: bread, eggs, cheese and fruit. The people at the desk are very friendly and they speak English. Only one thing is not good: the street is loud at night. I give four stars from five.

title: cats, dogs and buses
intro: Çoğul eki hep aynı yazılır ama üç ayrı ses verir: s, z ve iz. Hangisinin geleceğini önceki harf belirler.

tasks.de: The cats and the books are here.
tasks.hint: „cats“ ve „books“ sert sesle biter (t, k), bu yüzden ek „s“ okunur: kets, buks.

confusions.fix: Sert sessizden sonra ek titreşimsizdir: s sesi, z değil.

tasks.hint: „friends“ ve „dogs“ titreşimli sesle biter (n, g), bu yüzden ek „z“ okunur.

confusions.fix: Titreşimli sessizden sonra ek z olur: frendz, dogz.

tasks.de: The buses stop at the bridges.
tasks.hint: „bus“ ve „bridge“ ıslıklı sesle biter, bu yüzden araya bir hece girer: BA-siz, BRİ-ciz.

heard: The buss stop at the bridgs
confusions.fix: s ve c seslerinden sonra ek ayrı bir hecedir: -iz.

tasks.hint: Fiildeki -es de aynı kuralı izler: WO-şiz, Dİ-şiz. İki kez fazladan hece.

confusions.fix: „sh“ sesinden sonra ek ayrı hece olarak eklenir: -iz.

tasks.hint: „works“ ve „shops“ sert sesle bitiyor: wörks, şops. Ek s okunur.

confusions.fix: k ve p sert olduğu için ek de sert kalır: s.

tasks.de: The boxes are on the tables.
tasks.hint: „boxes“ fazladan hece alır (BOK-siz), „tables“ ise yalnız z sesiyle biter.

heard: The box are on the tablez
confusions.fix: x sesinden sonra -iz gelir; l sesinden sonra yalnız z.

tasks.hint: „watches“ ayrı hece alır (WO-çiz), „films“ ise z ile biter.

confusions.fix: „ch“ sesinden sonra -iz gelir: woçiz.

title: a, an, the — and some or any
intro: Türkçede olmayan üç küçük kelime ve Türkçeden farklı çalışan bir çoğul: ikisi birlikte öğrenilir.
focus: Çoğul biçimler, a / an / the ve some / any

explanation.heading: Çoğul: sayıdan sonra da eklenir
explanation.tr: Türkçede sayıdan sonra çoğul eki düşer: „iki kitap“. İngilizcede düşmez: two books. Ek genelde -s'tir; -s, -x, -ch, -sh ile bitenler -es alır; sessizden sonra -y gelen kelimeler -ies olur. Bir de ezberlenecek düzensizler var: child → children, man → men, foot → feet.

examples.de: two books, three cars
one box → two boxes
one city → two cities

explanation.heading: a, an, the
explanation.tr: Tekil sayılabilir bir şeyden ilk kez söz ederken „a“ gelir; kelime ünlü SESİYLE başlıyorsa „an“ olur. Karşındaki hangisi olduğunu biliyorsa „the“ kullanılır. Genel bir şey söylerken çoğulda artikel hiç konmaz.

examples.de: She is an engineer.
I need an umbrella.
I like books.

explanation.heading: some ve any
explanation.tr: Belirsiz bir miktar için olumlu cümlede „some“, olumsuz ve soruda „any“ kullanılır. Bir tek istisna vardır: teklif ve ricada soruda da „some“ gelir.

examples.de: There are some books here.
There isn't any milk.
Would you like some tea?

questions.text: I have two ___.
questions.explain: „child“ düzensizdir: çoğulu children'dır ve üzerine -s eklenmez.

questions.text: She is ___ engineer.
questions.explain: „engineer“ ünlü sesiyle başlar, bu yüzden „an“ gelir.

questions.text: We do not have ___ milk at home.
questions.explain: Olumsuz cümlede belirsiz miktar „any“ ile söylenir.

questions.text: Plural: one box → two ___
questions.explain: -x ile biten kelimeler -es alır: boxes.

questions.text: Plural: one city → two ___
questions.explain: Sessizden sonra gelen -y, -ies olur: cities.

questions.text: Would you like ___ tea?
questions.explain: Teklif ve ricada soruda da „some“ kullanılır.

questions.text: I need ___ umbrella.
questions.explain: „umbrella“ ünlü sesiyle başlıyor: an umbrella.

questions.text: Cümleyi doğru sıraya diz.
questions.explain: Olumlu cümlede belirsiz miktar „some“ ile gelir: There are some books here.

questions.text: „I have two childs.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: Doğrusu „two children“; bu kelimenin çoğulu düzensizdir.

questions.text: „I like music.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: Genel bir şeyden söz ediliyor ve „music“ sayılamaz; artikel gerekmez.

title: Bees on the Roof
intro: Şehirde arıcılık yapan biriyle üç soruluk kısa bir söyleşi okuyacaksın.
text:
BEES ON THE ROOF
Three questions for Ines Falk, city beekeeper

How did you start?
By accident. Four years ago a swarm sat on my balcony for two days. I called the fire service and they gave me the number of a beekeeper. He came, took the bees away and then said: “You are not afraid. Do you want to learn?”

Is the city really good for bees?
Better than most people think. In the country there are big fields with only one plant. Here we have gardens, parks and balconies, so the bees find something from March to October.

What is the hardest part?
The neighbors, not the bees. Before I put a hive on a roof, I talk to every flat in the building. It takes longer than the beekeeping, but after that nobody is worried.

title: going to or will?
intro: Türkçedeki tek gelecek eki İngilizcede ikiye ayrılır ve seçimi kararın ne zaman verildiği belirler.
focus: going to ve will

explanation.heading: Karar ne zaman verildi?
explanation.tr: Türkçede „arayacağım“ hem önceden planlanmış hem de o an verilmiş bir kararı anlatır. İngilizcede ikisi ayrılır: plan zaten varsa „be going to“, karar konuşma anında veriliyorsa „will“.

examples.de: I am going to call her tonight.
The phone is ringing. — I will answer it.
We are going to visit my aunt. We have the tickets.

explanation.heading: Tahminde de fark var
explanation.tr: Gözünle gördüğün bir işaretten yola çıkarak tahmin ediyorsan „going to“, yalnız düşüncene dayanıyorsan „will“ kullanılır.

examples.de: Look at those clouds! It is going to rain.
I think he will like the film.
Don't worry, it will be fine.

explanation.heading: Biçim
explanation.tr: „be going to“ üç parçadır: am / is / are + going to + yalın fiil. „will“ hiç değişmez ve arkasından yalın fiil gelir; kısa biçimi 'll, olumsuzu won't'tur. Söz verme ve teklif her zaman „will“ ile yapılır.

examples.de: She is going to start a new job.
I'll help you with that bag.
They won't come tomorrow.

questions.text: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
questions.explain: Görünen bir kanıt var (bulutlar), bu yüzden „going to“ gelir.

questions.text: The phone is ringing. — I ___ answer it.
questions.explain: Karar tam konuşma anında veriliyor: „will“.

questions.text: We ___ visit my aunt next weekend. We have the tickets.
questions.explain: Plan önceden yapılmış ve biletler alınmış: „going to“.

questions.text: I ___ (call) you tonight, I promise.
questions.explain: Söz verme her zaman „will“ ile yapılır.

questions.text: She ___ (start) a new job in June. She signed the contract last week.
questions.explain: Karar çoktan verilmiş ve sözleşme imzalanmış: be going to.

questions.text: It's cold in here. I ___ (close) the window.
questions.explain: Karar o anda alınıyor: will.

questions.text: They ___ (not / come) tomorrow. They told us last week.
questions.explain: Plan önceden bellidir, bu yüzden olumsuz biçim de „going to“ ile kurulur.

questions.text: Cümleyi doğru sıraya diz.
questions.explain: Sıra: özne + be + going to + yalın fiil: I am going to study tonight.

questions.text: „I will visit my sister next week; I bought the ticket yesterday.“ — En doğal biçim bu mu?
questions.explain: Bilet dün alınmış, yani plan önceden var; doğal biçim „I am going to visit my sister“.

questions.text: „I'll help you with that bag.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: Teklif konuşma anında yapılıyor ve „will“ ile kurulur; cümle doğru.

title: Quiet Hour at Marlow's
intro: Bir marketin sessiz saat uygulamasını anlatan bilgi yazısını okuyacaksın: ne değişiyor, kimin için, nasıl başladı.
text:
QUIET HOUR — EVERY TUESDAY, EIGHT TO NINE

From this month, Marlow's is a quieter shop for one hour every week.

What is different?
- No music and no announcements.
- The lights in the shop are lower.
- We do not fill the shelves during this hour, so there are no carts in the way.
- At the checkout, the machines do not beep. Our staff speak quietly.

Who is it for?
For everybody, but especially for people who find noise and bright light difficult: many autistic customers, people with a headache, older customers and parents with small babies.

Do I have to say anything?
No. Just come in and shop as usual.

We started this after a customer wrote to us in January. Twenty-two people answered her letter in one week. Thank you for the idea.

questions.text: What is a quiet hour?
options: one hour a week with less noise and light
an hour when the shop is closed
a special hour only for older people
questions.explain: „Marlow's is a quieter shop for one hour every week“ — müzik yok, ışıklar kısık.

questions.text: What is different at the checkout?
options: There is only one desk open.
questions.explain: „At the checkout, the machines do not beep. Our staff speak quietly.“

questions.explain: „We started this after a customer wrote to us in January.“

questions.text: Why do they not fill the shelves during this hour?
options: because the staff speak quietly then
because the carts are needed at the checkout
so that there are no carts in the way
questions.explain: „We do not fill the shelves during this hour, so there are no carts in the way.“

I can offer you two other times. Saturday at nine in the morning, or Monday at four in the afternoon.
Saturday is better if you want to practice on the highway. On Monday the traffic is heavier, which is also good practice, but slower.
Please text me before tomorrow evening. If I don't hear from you, I will keep Saturday for you.
And one more thing: bring your theory book. We will look at the road signs together for ten minutes.

title: Advice for a New Week
intro: Bir forumda ilk tam zamanlı işe başlayan birine tavsiye vereceksin; önce iki cümle kur, sonra cevabını yaz.

tasks.tr: Bana göre sabahlar akşamlardan daha sakin.

alternatives: The mornings are quieter than the evenings for me.
tasks.hint: Kısa sıfatlar -er alır ve karşılaştırmada „than“ gelir; „for me“ iki uçta da durabilir.

tasks.answer: Monday is the most difficult day for me.
alternatives: For me, Monday is the most difficult day.
tasks.hint: Uzun sıfatlar üstünlük derecesinde „the most“ ile kurulur.

tasks.prompt: Forumdaki soruya kendi deneyiminle cevap ver: haftan nasıl geçiyor, neler işe yaradı, ne işe yaramadı ve somut bir tavsiye ver.
tasks.stimulus: Hi everyone. I start my first full-time job next month and I am a bit afraid. I think I will have no time for cooking, sport or friends. How do you organize your week?
checklist: Duyguyu tanıdığını söyle
İşe yarayan iki şeyi anlat
İşe yaramayan bir şeyi söyle
Somut tek bir tavsiyeyle bitir

phrases.de: What did not work for me was …

tasks.sample: Hi, I remember that feeling very well. My first year was harder than I expected, but it got better. Two things helped me. First, I do all the shopping and cooking on Sunday afternoon. It takes three hours, but during the week I never stand in front of an empty fridge. Second, I put one evening in my calendar with nothing in it. If a friend asks, I say yes only if I still have another free evening. What did not work for me was getting up at five to study. I was just tired all day. My tip: choose one small thing and keep it for a month. Good luck!

title: The weak vowel
intro: İngilizcede vurgusuz heceler kısalır ve ünlüsü belirsiz bir „ı“ sesine döner; her heceyi net söylemek aksanı ağırlaştırır.

tasks.de: Can I have a banana, please?
tasks.hint: „a“ tek başına „ey“ değil, kısa bir „ı“dır. „banana“ = bı-NAA-nı.

confusions.fix: Yalnız ortadaki hece uzun; ilk ve son heceyi hafif „ı“ ile söyle.

tasks.hint: Sondaki -er hecesi „er“ değil, zayıf „ı“ gibidir: BRA-dı, TİİÇ-ı.

confusions.fix: Son heceyi vurgulama ve r'yi yuvarlama: bradı, tiiçı.

tasks.de: The children are at the cinema.
tasks.hint: „the“ = dı, „children“ = ÇİL-drın, „cinema“ = Sİ-nı-mı. Üçünde de zayıf ünlü var.

heard: Dee children are at dee cinema
confusions.fix: „the“ vurgusuzken „dii“ değil „dı“ okunur.

tasks.de: I was at the doctor on Monday.
tasks.hint: „was“ vurgusuzken „wız“ olur; „doctor“ = DOK-tı, „Monday“ = MAN-di.

confusions.fix: „was“ yardımcı olduğunda kısalır; sondaki -or da zayıflar.

tasks.hint: „can“ olumluda vurgusuzdur ve „kın“ okunur; „tomorrow“ = tı-MO-rou.

confusions.fix: „can“ olumlu cümlede zayıftır; vurgu asıl fiilde.

tasks.hint: „computers“ = kım-PYU-tız; ilk ve son hece zayıf, orta hece güçlü.

confusions.fix: İlk heceyi vurgulama; vurgu ortadaki „pu“ hecesinde.

title: bigger, the biggest
intro: Karşılaştırma İngilizcede ayrı bir kelimeyle değil, çoğu zaman sıfatın kendisine gelen eklerle kurulur.
focus: Comparatives ve superlatives

explanation.heading: Kısa sıfatlar: -er ve the -est
explanation.tr: Türkçede „daha büyük“ ve „en büyük“ ayrı kelimelerdir. İngilizcede tek ya da iki heceli sıfatlarda ek gelir: big → bigger → the biggest. Kısa ünlüden sonra son sessiz ikilenir (big → bigger), sonu -y olanlarda y düşer (happy → happier).

examples.de: This bag is bigger than mine.
Today is hotter than yesterday.
She is the happiest person here.

explanation.heading: Uzun sıfatlar: more ve the most
explanation.tr: Üç ve daha çok heceli sıfatlarda ek gelmez, önüne kelime gelir: expensive → more expensive → the most expensive. Ekle kelimeyi birlikte kullanmak („more bigger“) yaygın bir hatadır.

examples.de: This phone is more expensive.
It is the most interesting book in the series.
The film was more difficult than the book.

explanation.heading: Düzensizler ve eşitlik
explanation.tr: Dört sıfat kuralın dışındadır: good → better → the best, bad → worse → the worst, far → further, much/many → more → the most. Eşitlik için „as … as“ kullanılır: as tall as.

examples.de: This is the best day of the year.
The weather is worse than yesterday.
He is as tall as his brother.

questions.text: This bag is ___ than mine.
questions.explain: Tek heceli sıfat -er alır ve „than“ ile karşılaştırılır.

questions.text: It is the ___ restaurant in town.
questions.explain: Uzun sıfatlarda üstünlük derecesi „the most“ ile kurulur.

questions.text: Today is ___ than yesterday.
questions.explain: Kısa ünlüden sonra son sessiz ikilenir: hot → hotter.

questions.text: good → better → the ___
questions.explain: „good“ düzensizdir: good, better, the best.

questions.text: My sister is two years ___ (young) than me.
questions.explain: Tek heceli sıfat -er alır: younger than.

questions.text: This is the ___ (interesting) book in the series.
questions.explain: Dört heceli sıfat ek almaz: the most interesting.

questions.text: He is as tall ___ his brother.
questions.explain: Eşitlik „as … as“ ile kurulur; „than“ yalnız farkta kullanılır.

questions.text: Cümleyi doğru sıraya diz.
questions.explain: Üstünlük derecesi artikel ister: This is the best day.

questions.text: „This film is more better than the book.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: „better“ zaten karşılaştırma biçimidir; „more“ eklenmez.

questions.text: „Winter is colder than spring.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: Tek heceli sıfat -er almış ve „than“ doğru kullanılmış.

title: A Fridge on the Street
intro: Sokağa konmuş bir buzdolabını anlatan yerel haberi okuyacaksın: fikir kimden çıktı, kurallar neler, sonuç ne.
text:
A FRIDGE ON THE STREET

Since April there has been a fridge in front of the old post office in Mill Street. Anybody can put food in it, and anybody can take food out. Nobody has to explain why.

The idea came from a group of six people from the neighborhood. “We saw two things,” says Ola Brenner, one of them. “Shops throw away good food every evening, and some people in this street do not have enough. The fridge is the shortest way between the two.”

Three shops and one bakery bring things every day. There are rules: no meat, no fish, no open packets, and every person checks the date.

Two volunteers clean the fridge in the morning and in the evening. “Most days it is empty by eight,” says Ola. “That is not a problem. That is the answer.”

questions.text: What is the fridge for?
options: selling food that shops throw away
questions.explain: „Anybody can put food in it, and anybody can take food out.“

questions.text: What can you not put in the fridge?
questions.explain: „There are rules: no meat, no fish, no open packets …“

questions.text: Shops and a bakery bring food to the fridge every day.
questions.explain: „Three shops and one bakery bring things every day.“

questions.text: The fridge stands in front of the old ___ office.
questions.explain: „… a fridge in front of the old post office in Mill Street.“

questions.text: How often do volunteers clean the fridge?
questions.explain: „Two volunteers clean the fridge in the morning and in the evening.“

questions.text: What does Ola mean at the end?
options: An empty fridge shows that it works.
People take much more than they need.
The fridge is too small for the street.
questions.explain: „Most days it is empty by eight … That is not a problem. That is the answer.“

title: A Present for Kerem
intro: İki iş arkadaşı ayrılan bir meslektaşları için hazırlık yapıyor: ne alınacak, ne kadar toplanacak, kim ne yapacak.

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: Have you got a minute? It's about Kerem. His last day is on the twenty-eighth.

segments.speaker: Bruno
segments.text: Already? I thought he was leaving in July.

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: No, he found a flat there faster than he expected. So we have two weeks.

segments.speaker: Bruno
segments.text: Okay. Are we doing a present or just a card?

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: Both, I think. I asked around: most people want to give something for the garden. He talks about that balcony all the time.

segments.speaker: Bruno
segments.text: Good idea. How much do we collect?

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: Five euros from everybody. There are nineteen of us, so that is enough for the big pots and some soil.

segments.speaker: Bruno
segments.text: I can buy them on Saturday. My car is bigger than yours.

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: Perfect. Can you also write the card and put it on the table in the kitchen? People sign it during the week.

segments.speaker: Bruno
segments.text: Sure. And the cake?

segments.speaker: Ana
segments.text: Tuana is baking. Don't tell him anything, please.

questions.text: What are Ana and Bruno planning?
options: a present and a card for a colleague
a new balcony for the kitchen
a party for the whole office
questions.explain: „Are we doing a present or just a card?“ — „Both, I think.“

questions.text: When is Kerem's last day?
questions.explain: „His last day is on the twenty-eighth.“ Temmuz Bruno'nun yanlış hatırladığı tarih.

questions.text: They collect ten euros from everybody.
questions.explain: „Five euros from everybody.“

questions.text: What is Bruno going to buy?
questions.explain: „… that is enough for the big pots and some soil.“ — „I can buy them on Saturday.“

questions.text: Bruno'nun neden alışverişi üstlendiğini söylediği cümleyi duyduğun gibi yaz.
accept: My car is bigger than yours.
My car is bigger than yours
questions.explain: „My car is bigger than yours.“ — karşılaştırmada „than“ ve iyelik zamiri „yours“.

questions.text: What is Tuana doing?
questions.explain: „And the cake?“ — „Tuana is baking.“

title: Notes from the Meeting
intro: Toplantıya gelemeyen bir arkadaşın için kısa not yazacaksın; önce iki cümle kur, sonra notu yaz.

tasks.answer: There was too much information in the meeting.
alternatives: In the meeting there was too much information.
tasks.hint: „information“ sayılamaz: çoğulu yoktur ve „much“ ile kullanılır.

tasks.tr: Bu hafta çok fazla toplantımız var.
tasks.answer: This week we have too many meetings.
alternatives: We have too many meetings this week.
tasks.hint: Sayılabilen isimlerde „many“, sayılamayanlarda „much“ kullanılır.

tasks.prompt: Bir iş arkadaşın toplantıya gelemedi. Ona kısa not yaz: kimler vardı, hangi kararlar alındı, hangi soru açık kaldı, son tarihler neler ve ondan ne bekleniyor.
checklist: Kimlerin olduğunu ve kimin olmadığını yaz
En az üç kararı numaralayarak yaz
Açık kalan soruyu ve kimin ilgileneceğini söyle
Son tarihi ve ondan isteneni yaz
tasks.sample: Hi Marta, here are my notes from Tuesday. Nine people were there; Kerem and you were not. We decided three things. First, the summer party is on the twelfth of July, in the garden, not in the canteen. Second, we buy two new printers, one for each floor. Third, the Friday meeting starts at nine now, not at half past eight. One question is still open: nobody knows how much money is left for the training. Nina is going to ask the office on Monday. The deadline for the party list is the twentieth of June. Please send your holiday dates to Ali before Friday. That was everything important!

title: Letters you do not say
intro: İngilizcede yazılan her harf okunmaz; bu sessiz harfler kelimelerin en sık tanınmama nedenidir.

tasks.hint: „know“ baştaki k okunmaz: nou. „answer“ ortadaki w de okunmaz: AAN-sır.

tasks.hint: „write“ baştaki w okunmaz: rayt. Aynı kural „wrong“ ve „wrist“ için de geçerli.

confusions.fix: wr- ile başlayan kelimelerde w sessizdir: rayt.

tasks.hint: „half“ içindeki l okunmaz: haaf. „hour“ baştaki h de okunmaz: auır.

confusions.fix: „half“ta l yok, „hour“da h yok: haaf ın auır.

tasks.de: Listen! Somebody is at the door.
tasks.hint: „listen“ ortadaki t okunmaz: Lİ-sın. Aynısı „castle“ ve „often“ için de olur.

confusions.fix: st- birleşiminde t düşer: lisın.

tasks.hint: „island“ içindeki s okunmaz: AY-lınd.

confusions.fix: Baştaki i uzun „ay“, arkasından gelen s ise hiç duyulmaz.

title: much, many and a lot of
intro: Türkçedeki tek „çok“ İngilizcede ikiye ayrılır ve bazı isimler hiç çoğul olmaz.
focus: Sayılabilen ve sayılamayan isimler, much / many

explanation.heading: İki tür isim
explanation.tr: Türkçede „üç bilgi“ demek sorun değildir. İngilizcede bazı isimler sayılamaz: çoğul olmazlar ve önlerine a / an gelmez. Sık kullanılanlar: information, advice, money, bread, water, work, news, furniture.

examples.de: She gave me a lot of advice.
I need some information.
There is a lot of work today.

explanation.heading: many, much ve a lot of
explanation.tr: Sayılabilenlerin çoğuluyla „many“, sayılamayanlarla „much“ kullanılır. „a lot of“ ikisiyle de gider ve olumlu cümlede en doğal seçimdir; „much“ daha çok soruda ve olumsuzda görülür.

examples.de: How many people were there?
I don't have much time.
We have a lot of books.

explanation.heading: Sayma birimleri
explanation.tr: Sayılamayan bir şeyi saymak istiyorsan araya bir birim koyarsın: a piece of advice, a slice of bread, a bottle of water, two pieces of information.

examples.de: Can I have a bottle of water?
He gave me one piece of advice.
I ate two slices of bread.

questions.text: How ___ people were there?
questions.explain: „people“ sayılabilir bir çoğuldur, bu yüzden „many“ gelir.

questions.text: I don't have ___ time this week.
questions.explain: „time“ burada sayılamaz ve cümle olumsuz: much.

questions.text: She gave me a lot of ___.
questions.explain: „advice“ sayılamaz: çoğul olmaz ve artikel almaz.

questions.text: How ___ money do you need?
questions.explain: „money“ sayılamaz, bu yüzden „much“ kullanılır.

questions.text: There isn't ___ bread left.
questions.explain: „bread“ sayılamaz ve cümle olumsuz: much.

questions.text: We have too ___ chairs in this room.
questions.explain: „chairs“ sayılabilir bir çoğuldur: many.

questions.text: Can I have a ___ of water, please?
questions.explain: Sayılamayan bir şeyi saymak için araya bir birim girer: a bottle of water.

questions.text: Soruyu doğru sıraya diz.
questions.explain: Soru kelimesi öbeği başta, sonra yardımcı fiil ve özne: How many books do you have?

questions.text: „He gave me three informations.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: „information“ sayılamaz; doğrusu „three pieces of information“.

questions.text: „There is a lot of work today.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: „work“ sayılamaz ve „a lot of“ ikisiyle de kullanılabilir; cümle doğru.

title: What Do You Do With Your Old Phone?
intro: Bir forumda eski telefonların ne yapıldığı soruluyor; soruyu ve üç farklı cevabı okuyacaksın.
text:
FORUM: WHAT DO YOU DO WITH YOUR OLD PHONE?

Question from Nils:
My old phone still works, but the battery is bad and it is slow. It is in a drawer with two others. What do you do with yours?

Selin:
I sold mine on a second-hand site. It took three weeks and a lot of messages, but I got sixty euros. Important: delete everything first and take the card out. I forgot that once.

Marcus:
A new battery cost me thirty euros and now my phone is four years old and fine. If you have a repair café near you, go there. They also tell you if it is not worth it.

Rana:
Ours go to my mother. She uses one phone until it stops working completely. My old one is now in Izmir, and it takes better photos than her new one.

questions.text: What is the question in this forum?
options: what to do with an old phone
questions.explain: Başlık ve Nils'in son cümlesi aynı soruyu soruyor: „What do you do with yours?“

questions.text: What does Selin say is important?
options: delete everything and take the card out
sell the phone in three weeks
questions.explain: „Important: delete everything first and take the card out.“

questions.text: Marcus bought a new phone.
questions.explain: „A new battery cost me thirty euros and now my phone is four years old and fine.“

questions.text: A new battery cost Marcus ___ euros.
questions.explain: „A new battery cost me thirty euros …“

questions.explain: „My old one is now in Izmir, and it takes better photos than her new one.“

questions.text: What does the repair café also do?
options: It takes all the old phones away.
It says when a repair is not worth it.
questions.explain: „They also tell you if it is not worth it.“

title: A Café Without Phones
intro: Telefonsuz bir kafeyi işleten kadınla söyleşi dinleyeceksin: kural nasıl işliyor, neden başladı, sonuç ne.

segments.speaker: Reporter
segments.text: You have a sign on the door: no phones. Is that a joke?

segments.speaker: Ilva
segments.text: No, it's real. But it is not a rule with a punishment. Nobody takes your phone away.

segments.speaker: Reporter
segments.text: So what happens if I take mine out?

segments.speaker: Ilva
segments.text: Nothing. Somebody comes and brings you a small wooden box for the table. Most people laugh and put the phone in.

segments.speaker: Reporter
segments.text: Why did you start this?

segments.speaker: Ilva
segments.text: Because of the noise. Not the loud noise, the other one: twenty people alone at twenty tables. It was very quiet and very sad.

segments.speaker: Reporter
segments.text: And now?

segments.speaker: Ilva
segments.text: Now it is louder. People talk to the people at the next table. We also lost customers, that is true. Some come for work and need a screen.

segments.speaker: Reporter
segments.text: Would you do it again?

segments.speaker: Ilva
segments.text: Yes, but I would explain it better at the beginning. In the first month people thought we were against something. We are for something.

questions.text: What is the rule in the café?
options: You cannot bring a phone in.
You do not use your phone.
You pay more if you use a phone.
questions.explain: „It is not a rule with a punishment. Nobody takes your phone away.“ — telefon içeri girebiliyor, kullanılmıyor.

questions.text: What happens if you take your phone out?
options: The sign on the door is explained to you.
You are asked to sit at the next table.
questions.explain: „Somebody comes and brings you a small wooden box for the table.“

questions.text: Ilva would introduce the rule again.
questions.explain: „Would you do it again?“ — „Yes, but I would explain it better at the beginning.“

questions.text: Why did Ilva start this?
questions.explain: „Because of the noise. Not the loud noise, the other one …“

questions.text: Ilva'nın son cümlesini duyduğun gibi yaz.
questions.explain: „We are for something.“ — bir önceki cümledeki „against“ ile karşıtlık kuruyor.

questions.text: What would Ilva do differently?
options: explain the idea better at the start
open a second café in the town
questions.explain: „… but I would explain it better at the beginning.“

title: Handover Letter
intro: Gönüllü olduğun işi devrediyorsun; önce iki cümle kur, sonra devralacak kişiye bir mektup yaz.

tasks.tr: Vardiya salı günü saat beşte başlıyor.
tasks.answer: The shift starts at five on Tuesday.
alternatives: On Tuesday the shift starts at five.
tasks.hint: Saat için „at“, gün için „on“, ay ve yıl için „in“ kullanılır.

tasks.answer: I am moving to Portugal next month.
alternatives: Next month I am moving to Portugal.
tasks.hint: Kesinleşmiş bir plan için şimdiki zaman biçimi gelecek anlamı taşır.

tasks.prompt: Gönüllü olduğun işi devrediyorsun. Devralacak kişiye mektup yaz: vardiya ne zaman, anahtar kimde, ilk ne yapılmalı, sık çıkan bir aksaklık ve kime ulaşılacağı. Sıcak bir kapanış yaz.
checklist: Vardiya gününü ve saatini yaz
Anahtarın kimde olduğunu söyle

tasks.sample: Dear Ferhat, welcome to the Thursday team! Here is everything I know. The shift starts at five on Tuesday and Thursday and finishes at eight. The key is with Mrs. Lang in flat two; she is at home after four. First, turn on the two heaters in the back room, because it takes an hour to get warm. The coffee machine often stops in the middle. Do not open it; just turn it off and on again. If something is really broken, call Deniz on 0176 33 88 12. She answers late in the evening too. I am moving to Portugal next month, but write to me if you have questions. Good luck!

title: Words that hold hands
intro: İngilizcede kelimeler tek tek değil, birbirine bağlanarak söylenir; bu yüzden bildiğin kelimeleri duymak zorlaşır.

tasks.hint: Sessizle biten kelime ünlüyle başlayan kelimeye yapışır: pi-ki-tap.

confusions.fix: Üç kelimeyi ayrı ayrı söyleme; tek bir öbek gibi bağla.

confusions.fix: „of“ vurgusuzdur ve önceki kelimeye yapışır: kapıv tii.

title: at, on, in — and plans
intro: Zaman edatlarının üçü de Türkçede „-de“ ile karşılanır; hangisinin geleceğini zaman biriminin büyüklüğü belirler.
focus: Zaman edatları ve gelecek için present continuous

explanation.heading: Küçükten büyüğe: at, on, in
explanation.tr: Türkçede hepsi „-de“ ekidir: beşte, salıda, mayısta. İngilizcede zaman birimi büyüdükçe edat değişir: saat için „at“, gün ve tarih için „on“, ay, mevsim ve yıl için „in“.

examples.de: The film starts at half past eight.
My birthday is on the fifth of May.
We are going to Rome in July.

explanation.heading: Ezberlenecek birkaç istisna
explanation.tr: Günün bölümleri „in“ alır (in the morning, in the afternoon), ama „at night“ ve „at noon“ istisnadır. Amerikan kullanımında hafta sonu „on the weekend“tir.

examples.de: She works better in the morning.
I don't drive at night.
We are free on the weekend.

explanation.heading: Plan için şimdiki zaman
explanation.tr: Kesinleşmiş bir randevu ya da bilet için gelecek zaman yerine present continuous kullanılır. Cümlede bir zaman ifadesi bulunması gerekir, yoksa cümle „şu an“ anlaşılır.

examples.de: I am meeting Ali at six tonight.
examples.tr: Bu akşam altıda Ali ile buluşuyorum.

examples.de: We are flying to Rome tomorrow.
She is starting her new job on Monday.

questions.text: The meeting is ___ Monday.
questions.explain: Gün adlarıyla „on“ kullanılır.

questions.text: I get up ___ seven o'clock.
questions.explain: Saatle „at“ kullanılır.

questions.text: We are going to Rome ___ July.
questions.explain: Ay adlarıyla „in“ kullanılır.

questions.text: The film starts ___ half past eight.
questions.explain: Saat bildiren ifadelerde „at“ gelir.

questions.text: My birthday is ___ the fifth of May.
questions.explain: Tam bir tarih verildiğinde „on“ kullanılır.

questions.text: I ___ (meet) Ali at six tonight.
questions.explain: Randevu kesinleşmiş; plan için present continuous kullanılır.

questions.text: She works better ___ the morning.
questions.explain: Günün bölümleri „in the“ alır: in the morning.

questions.text: „I am meeting the doctor at four tomorrow.“ — Bu cümle doğru mu?
questions.explain: Randevu var ve zaman ifadesi verilmiş; plan için doğru biçim.

questions.explain: Gün adıyla „on“ gelir; doğrusu „The party is on Saturday.“

title: The Night the Town Turned Off Its Lights
intro: Bir kasabanın sokak lambalarını doksan dakika söndürdüğü geceyi anlatan haberi okuyacaksın: fikir kimden çıktı, ne ölçüldü, sonra ne olacak.
text:
THE NIGHT THE TOWN TURNED OFF ITS LIGHTS

For ninety minutes last Friday, most of Halden was dark. Between ten and half past eleven the council switched off the street lights in four areas, and around six hundred people came out to look up.

The idea came from a group of teachers at the secondary school. “If you ask children to draw the night sky, they draw six or seven stars,” says Kari Lund, who teaches physics. “That is what they see. If they lived thirty kilometers from here, they would draw hundreds.”

The evening was not only about stars. Two engineers from the council used the time to measure how much light the town sends upwards. Their first result: about a third of it does not light anything at all. It goes past the road and into the sky, because the lamps are old and have no cover on top.

“If we changed those lamps, we would use less electricity and see more sky,” said one of them. “The problem is that nobody notices the light we waste. You cannot see what is missing.”

The council will decide in November. Until then, the group is asking people a simple question: if your street were darker, would you feel less safe, or would you just see better?

questions.text: What happened last Friday?
options: The council cut the electricity to save money.
A school organized a trip to see the stars.
The town turned off some street lights for an evening.
questions.explain: „… the council switched off the street lights in four areas, and around six hundred people came out to look up.“

questions.text: What did the two engineers measure?
options: how much light goes into the sky
how bright the stars above the town are
how many people came out that evening
questions.explain: „… used the time to measure how much light the town sends upwards.“

questions.text: The idea for the evening came from teachers.
questions.explain: „The idea came from a group of teachers at the secondary school.“

questions.text: About ___ of the light does not light anything at all.
questions.explain: „Their first result: about a third of it does not light anything at all.“

questions.text: When will the council decide?
questions.explain: „The council will decide in November.“

questions.text: Why does the engineer say nobody notices the waste?
options: Because you cannot see light that is missing.
Because the council does not publish numbers.
Because the lamps are already very old.
questions.explain: „The problem is that nobody notices the light we waste. You cannot see what is missing.“

title: A Free Year
intro: Bir podcast üç kişiye aynı soruyu soruyor: bir yıl boyunca masrafların karşılansaydı ne yapardın?

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Welcome back. Today's question is simple and impossible: if somebody paid your rent and your bills for one year, what would you do?

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: We asked three people. First, Tomas, who is twenty-six and works in a warehouse.

segments.speaker: Tomas
segments.text: Everybody expects me to say travel. I wouldn't. I would finish the electrician course I stopped four years ago. If I had that certificate, my whole life would look different in ten years.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Second, Ruth, sixty-one, a nurse for thirty years.

segments.speaker: Ruth
segments.text: I would sleep. Honestly. And then, after about a month, I would be bored and I would go back two days a week. If I stopped completely, I think I would lose something.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: And third, Amal, who is thirty-four and has two small children.

segments.speaker: Amal
segments.text: People always ask what you would do. Nobody asks what you would stop doing. I would stop apologizing for being late everywhere.

segments.speaker: Amal
segments.text: If I had the time, I would just be on time, and that would change more than any big plan.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Three answers, and not one of them is a holiday. Next week we ask the opposite question: what would you do if you had one week and no money?

questions.text: What is the question in this episode?
options: how people usually spend their holidays
what people would do with a paid free year
why people change jobs after thirty
questions.explain: „… if somebody paid your rent and your bills for one year, what would you do?“

questions.text: What would Tomas do?
options: work fewer days in the warehouse
questions.explain: „I would finish the electrician course I stopped four years ago.“

questions.text: Ruth would stop working completely.
questions.explain: „… I would go back two days a week. If I stopped completely, I think I would lose something.“

questions.text: What would Amal stop doing?
questions.explain: „I would stop apologizing for being late everywhere.“

questions.text: Amal'ın herkesin sormadığı soruyu anlattığı cümleyi duyduğun gibi yaz.
accept: Nobody asks what you would stop doing.
Nobody asks what you would stop doing
questions.explain: „Nobody asks what you would stop doing.“ — dolaylı soru düz cümle sırasıyla kurulur.

questions.text: What does the host notice at the end?
questions.explain: „Three answers, and not one of them is a holiday.“

title: A Terrace on the Roof?
intro: Apartmanın forumunda çatı terası tartışılıyor; önce iki cümle kur, sonra gerekçeli katkını yaz.

tasks.tr: Herkes katılırsa maliyet daire başına iki bin euro olacak.
tasks.answer: If everybody joins, the cost will be two thousand euros per flat.
alternatives: The cost will be two thousand euros per flat if everybody joins.
tasks.hint: Birinci tip koşulda „if“ yarısı geniş zaman, ana yarısı „will“ alır.

tasks.tr: Terası ben planlasaydım, işe gölgeyle başlardım.
tasks.answer: If I planned the terrace, I would start with shade.
alternatives: I would start with shade if I planned the terrace.
tasks.hint: İkinci tip koşulda „if“ yarısı geçmiş biçim, ana yarısı „would“ alır.

tasks.prompt: Apartmanının forumunda çatı terası öneriliyor. Katkını yaz: net bir tutum al, iki gerekçe ver, bir şart koy, haklı bulduğun bir itirazı kabul et ve somut bir öneriyle bitir.
tasks.stimulus: Proposal for the owners' meeting: we want to open the roof as a shared terrace. Estimated cost: twenty-four thousand euros for the railing, the door and the floor, shared between the twelve flats. Please write your opinion before the thirtieth of April.
checklist: Tutumunu ilk cümlede söyle
İki gerekçe ver ve birini örnekle
Bir şart koy ve nedenini açıkla
Bir itirazı kabul et ve somut öneriyle bitir

phrases.de: I also accept the objection about …
phrases.tr: … ile ilgili itirazı da kabul ediyorum

tasks.sample: I am in favor, but only with one condition. Two reasons first. If we open the roof, the building gets a real common space for the first time; at the moment the only place we meet is the letter boxes. And a terrace is worth more than a new front door, both for us now and if somebody sells later. My condition is the noise. If there are no times written down, the flats on the top floor will pay for everybody's summer. I would put quiet hours from ten at night in the same paper as the costs. I also accept the objection about money: two thousand euros is a lot in one year. If the payment were spread over three years, I think most of us could manage it. So: yes to the terrace, with quiet hours and with instalments.

title: One Extra Hour
intro: Bir dakikaya yakın tek başına konuşacaksın: bir seçim yap, gerekçelendir ve neyi seçmediğini de söyle.

monologue.promptTr: Her günün yirmi beş saat olsaydı, o fazladan saati neye ayırırdın? Seçimini söyle, en az iki gerekçeyle destekle ve akla gelen bir seçeneği neden seçmediğini açıkla.
bulletsTr: Seçimini tek cümleyle söyle
İki gerekçe ver, biri somut olsun
Akla ilk gelen seçeneği neden seçmediğini söyle
Kısa bir sonuçla bitir

targets.de: If I had one extra hour, I would …
The first reason is …
Of course I could say …
But if I am honest, …

monologue.sampleDe: If I had one extra hour every day, I would not use it for work, and I would not use it for sport either. I would use it for cooking. The first reason is simple: at the moment I cook badly and fast, and I eat the same four things. If I had an hour, I would learn to cook properly, and after a year that is three hundred and sixty-five meals. The second reason is that cooking is the only thing I do where nothing else can happen at the same time; my phone is in the other room because my hands are wet, and that is rare now. Of course I could say sleep, and my doctor would agree. But if I am honest, I would waste an extra hour of sleep by going to bed later. An hour in the kitchen is harder to waste.
monologue.rubricHint: İkinci tip koşul beklenir (If I had …, I would …); en az iki gerekçe ve reddedilen bir seçenek bulunmalı.

title: if I go and if I went
intro: Aynı „if“ kelimesi iki ayrı dünyayı kurar: biri gerçekten olabilecek, öteki yalnız hayal edilen.
focus: Conditionals 1 ve 2

explanation.heading: Gerçek olan: birinci tip
explanation.tr: Türkçede „yağarsa kalırız“ dersin. İngilizcede aynı yapı iki parçadır: „if“ yarısında geniş zaman, ana yarıda „will“. Bu tip gerçekten olabilecek bir gelecek için kullanılır.

examples.de: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
If you leave now, you will catch the bus.
We will call you if there is a problem.

explanation.heading: Hayal olan: ikinci tip
explanation.tr: Gerçekleşmesi uzak ya da imkânsız bir durumda „if“ yarısında geçmiş biçim, ana yarıda „would“ kullanılır. Geçmiş biçim burada zaman değil, uzaklık gösterir — Türkçedeki „-seydi“ gibi.

examples.de: If I had more money, I would buy a bigger flat.
examples.tr: Daha çok param olsa daha büyük bir daire alırdım.

examples.de: If she knew the answer, she would tell us.
If I were you, I would ask her.

explanation.heading: İki sık hata
explanation.tr: Birincisi: „if“ yarısında „will“ kullanılmaz — „If it will rain“ yanlıştır. İkincisi: virgül yalnız „if“ yarısı önce geldiğinde konur; sona gelirse virgül yoktur.

examples.de: If it rains, we will stay at home.
We will stay at home if it rains.

title: What Happens to Your Suitcase
intro: Havalimanında bagajın izlediği yolu anlatan bir yazı okuyacaksın: hangi adımlar var, ne zaman insan devreye giriyor.
text:
WHAT HAPPENS TO YOUR SUITCASE

Between the moment your bag is taken at the desk and the moment it appears in another country, it travels about two kilometers and is touched by almost nobody.

First a label is printed and stuck on the handle. The label carries a code, and everything after that is done by that code, not by your name. The bag is put on a belt and disappears through a rubber curtain.

Below the terminal, it is photographed from six sides. If the code cannot be read, the bag is sent to a small room where a person reads it by hand. About one bag in three hundred ends up there.

Then it is sorted. In a large airport the bags are pushed onto separate lines by little arms; each line belongs to one flight. Bags for early flights are stored in a cold hall, sometimes for several hours.

Finally the bags are loaded into containers and driven to the plane. This is the only part where a human decision is still made every time: somebody must check that the container is closed correctly.

Most lost bags are not lost. They are simply late, because they missed one of these steps and were put on the next flight. Nine out of ten are returned within two days.

title: Where Your Water Comes From

segments.text: Good evening, and thank you for coming. In the next twenty minutes I will show you what happens to the water between the ground and your kitchen.
The first surprise is the distance. Our water is not taken from the river you can see from here. It is pumped from a layer of sand about forty meters below us.
That sand is already a filter. Water that goes in at the top of the hill is not used for about nine years.
In the works, four things are done. First, the water is aerated: it falls through the air so that iron comes out of it.
Second, it is filtered through sand again. Third, in dry summers a small amount of chlorine is added. And fourth, it is tested, every day, in that room behind me.
We take fifty samples a week. Nothing is sent out before it has been checked twice by two different people.
And the last thing, because I am always asked: no, the water is not made softer here. That is done in your house, or not at all.
Now, if you follow me, the pumps are through this door. Please stay behind the yellow line.

phrases.de: Everybody asked me the same question.

tasks.sample: I worked on the night desk of a small hotel for three months, from eleven at night to seven in the morning. Everybody asked me the same question: what do you actually do? Here is the honest answer. About two hours of the night are work. The accounts are closed at half past one, the breakfast lists are printed, and the door is opened at six in the morning. The rest is waiting. The surprise was who comes down at three o'clock. Not the loud guests; they sleep. It is people who cannot sleep, and they want to talk to somebody who is not their family. I was never trained for that part, and it was the part I did most. The hard part was the second day off: the first day you sleep, and on the second you are awake at four in the morning in a flat where nothing is open. Would I do it again? Yes, but not in winter.

monologue.sampleDe: I think they should, but not in the way it is usually done. The strongest argument is simple and it is not about medicine. In an emergency most people do nothing, and they do nothing because they are afraid of making it worse. That fear is not removed by one afternoon at the age of sixteen; it is removed by doing the same thing every year until it feels normal. Against this, people say the timetable is already full, and they are right. But first aid does not need a whole subject. Twenty minutes, three times a year, would be enough if it is always the same three things: call, check, press. My only condition is that it must be practical. If it is taught from a book and tested on paper, we will get students who can name the steps and still stand still, and that is worse than nothing, because it looks like a solution.

text:
NOTES FROM THE MEETING — FOURTEENTH OF MARCH
For members who could not come

Forty-one people were at the meeting in the old school. Here is what was said and what was decided.

Mrs. Ferreira opened the meeting and explained that the shop had closed in November and that the owner did not want to sell to another shop. She said that the building was for sale for one hundred and ten thousand euros.

Bahar Kaya, who runs the bakery van, said that she brought bread to the village three days a week and that she could add two more days if there was somewhere to stop. She asked whether the group had thought about a smaller solution first.

Two members disagreed. Mr. Lang said that a van was not a shop, because you could not go there when you needed one thing. He added that the last two villages that had lost their shops had also lost their bus stops within five years.

The vote: thirty-three people said that they would put in five hundred euros each; six were against; two did not vote.

Decisions. First, a working group of five people will ask the bank about a loan before the end of April. Second, Bahar Kaya will try two extra days from May. These two are not alternatives.

monologue.sampleDe: I would not choose between them, because they do different jobs. Apps are better at telling me that something happened; people are better at telling me whether it matters. If a bridge is closed, I want that from an app, in ten seconds, with a map. But last year the school in our street changed its hours, and I found out from a neighbor at the letter boxes, three weeks before the letter came. No app knew, because nobody had written it down. The problem with people is that they tell you what they are interested in, and the problem with apps is that they tell you what keeps you looking. title: If You Lose Your Documents Abroad
intro: Yurt dışında belgesini kaybedenler için bir rehber okuyacaksın: ilk saatte ne yapılmalı, neyi ödemek zorunda değilsin.
text:
IF YOU LOSE YOUR DOCUMENTS ABROAD

Losing a passport is not an emergency, but the first hour matters more than the next three days.

You have to report the loss twice: once to the local police and once to your embassy or consulate. The police report is the document that everything else is built on, so get it before you do anything else. In most countries you must go in person; a phone call is not enough.

You should take a photo of your passport now, before you travel, and send it to yourself by email. A photo is not a legal document, but it saves hours at the consulate, because the number is on it.

At the consulate you will normally get an emergency travel document. It is valid for one journey home and for a fixed number of days. You must not use it for a holiday in a third country; that is a common and expensive mistake.

You do not have to pay for everything yourself. Many travel insurance policies cover the fee and the extra nights, but almost all of them require the police report within twenty-four hours. Read that line before you buy the policy, not after.

And one small thing that people forget: your bank cards. They should be blocked before you go to bed, not the next morning.

tasks.sample: Dear Mira, I am very glad you are going, and I am going to be annoying for exactly one page. Three things you have to do. First, make a copy of your passport and your insurance and put it somewhere that is not your bag. Second, tell one person at home your address for each night; not a plan, just where you sleep. Third, keep some cash separate from your card, because cards stop working at the worst moment, usually on a Sunday. monologue.sampleDe: I would not choose a subject, because subjects are the wrong unit. I would choose one skill: how to read a contract. That sounds narrow, and that is why I like it. Everybody signs something before they are twenty: a phone contract, a rental agreement, a first job. Most people sign without reading, not because they are lazy, but because nobody has ever shown them which four lines actually matter. It should be taught the way swimming is taught: with a real document, in a real room, with somebody next to you. People say schools should teach cooking or taxes, and I agree that both are useful. But you can learn to cook from a friend, and tax rules change every few years. The habit of reading before signing lasts.

title: must, should and have to

title: The Building That Was Easier to Knock Down
intro: Eski binaların neden yıkıldığını sorgulayan bir deneme okuyacaksın: hesap nasıl kuruluyor, neyi dışarıda bırakıyor.
text:
THE BUILDING THAT WAS EASIER TO KNOCK DOWN

Every town has one: a solid, ordinary building from the nineteen sixties that everybody agrees is ugly and nobody quite dares to defend. When it comes down, the reason given is almost always the same — it was cheaper to demolish than to convert. That sentence sounds like a fact. It is a result.

Start with the numbers that are usually quoted. A conversion, which has to work around what is already there, is unpredictable; a new build, which starts from an empty site, can be priced to the euro. Banks, whose job is to dislike surprises, lend more easily against the second. So the comparison is not between two costs. It is between a cost and a guess.

Then there is the part that appears in no column at all. A building that is demolished takes its embodied carbon with it: the energy that was spent making the concrete, which was released decades ago and can never be recovered. A study of forty projects in three countries found that a conversion which is thirty per cent more expensive on paper is usually cheaper once that carbon is counted at any realistic price.

None of this means that every old building should be kept. There are structures whose floors cannot carry modern services and whose windows cannot be enlarged without taking the walls apart. Architects who work in this field are the first to say so.

The point is narrower. When we say that a building was not worth saving, we usually mean that our way of counting made it look that way. That is a decision about accounting, and decisions about accounting can be changed — which is exactly what makes them worth arguing about.

questions.text: What is the writer's main claim?
options: New buildings are always cheaper to build.
Old buildings should almost always be kept.
The cost comparison is shaped by how we count.
questions.explain: „That sentence sounds like a fact. It is a result“ ve son paragraf aynı şeyi söylüyor.

questions.text: Why do banks prefer a new build?

It is always cheaper in the end.
questions.explain: „Banks, whose job is to dislike surprises, lend more easily against the second.“

questions.text: What does the last paragraph suggest?
options: Architects alone should make the decision.
The rules of accounting can be argued about.
Demolition should be forbidden by law.
questions.explain: „… decisions about accounting can be changed — which is exactly what makes them worth arguing about.“

title: Opt In or Opt Out?
intro: Bir podcast bölümünde varsayılan kuralın etkisi tartışılıyor: yasa ne kadar değiştiriyor, asıl darboğaz nerede.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: This week: a change that costs almost nothing, takes one line of law, and divides people completely. Should organ donation be opt-out?

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: In an opt-in country, you are not a donor unless you say yes. In an opt-out country, you are a donor unless you say no. My guest is Dr. Ines Wall, who has studied both systems for fifteen years.

segments.speaker: Ines
segments.text: The first thing to say is that the effect is real but smaller than the headlines. Countries that switched saw an increase, but the ones which increased most were those that also paid for more coordinators in hospitals.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: So the law is not the main thing?

segments.speaker: Ines
segments.text: The law is the thing that makes the conversation happen. In practice, families are still asked, and a family who has never discussed it will usually say no. That is the actual bottleneck, and it is not legal.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: What about the objection that opt-out takes something away from people?

segments.speaker: Ines
segments.text: I take it seriously, and the answer depends on how easy it is to opt out.

segments.speaker: Ines
segments.text: A system where you have to write a letter is not the same as one where you tick a box when you renew your driving license.

segments.speaker: Ines
segments.text: If I could change one thing, it would not be the law. It would be that every adult is asked once, clearly, in a place where they are not in a hurry.

segments.speaker: Host

title: Who Pays for Free Returns?
intro: Bir gazete için kısa bir köşe yazısı yazacaksın; önce iki cümle kur, sonra yorumu yaz.

alternatives: The customers who never send anything back pay the difference in the end.
tasks.hint: Tanımlayıcı ilgi cümlesi virgülsüzdür ve isimden hemen sonra gelir; zaman öbeği iki uçta durabilir.

alternatives: The shop that I mentioned has shown the return rates since last year.

tasks.prompt: İnternetten alışverişte ücretsiz iade üzerine köşe yazısı yaz: gözlemini somut anlat, bedelini gerçekte kimin ödediğini göster, karşı tarafın en güçlü argümanını kabul et ve tek bir somut öneriyle bitir.

phrases.tr: İnternette hiçbir şey gerçekten bedava değil.

phrases.de: The argument for … is stronger than it looks.
A charge that looks fair on paper …
phrases.tr: Kâğıt üstünde adil görünen bir ücret …

phrases.de: So the answer is not …, it is …
The only reason we do not see them is …

tasks.sample:
Nothing online is really free, and returns are the clearest example. A coat that is ordered in three sizes and sent back in two has been driven twice, handled four times and, in about a quarter of cases, never sold again. The customers who never send anything back pay the difference, quietly, in the price of everything else.

The argument for keeping free returns is stronger than it looks. Buying clothes you cannot try on is a gamble, and a fee would fall hardest on the people who cannot easily get to a shop: those who live far out, those who work shifts, those who are not the size the industry designs for. A charge that looks fair on paper is not fair on a Tuesday in a village.

So the answer is not a flat fee, it is information. The shop that I mentioned above now shows, on the product page, how often each item is returned and why. Sales of the worst items fell by a third in six months, and nobody had to be charged anything. Shops already know these numbers. The only reason we do not see them is that nobody has been made to show them.

title: Whose Name on the Building?
intro: Bir buçuk dakikaya kadar konuşacaksın: iki tarafı da tart, sonra kendi ölçütünü ayrıştırarak koy.

monologue.promptTr: Kamu binalarına ve spor tesislerine sponsor adı verilmeli mi? İki tarafın da en güçlü argümanını söyle, sonra hangi durumda ne yapılması gerektiğini ayır.

Sponsorluk lehine en güçlü argümanı söyle

monologue.sampleDe: The question is usually asked as a question about money, but it is really about who a building belongs to. The strongest argument in favor is simple and I do not want to skip it: a name on a stand can pay for the stand, and clubs that refuse sponsorship often end up charging their own members instead. That is not a free choice; it is a different bill sent to poorer people. Against that, a name is not just money. A hall that is named after a company teaches everybody who walks past it that public space is for sale, and the sentence lasts longer than the contract, which is usually five years. My criterion would be the difference between a room and an institution. Sell the name of a stand, a scoreboard or a summer tournament for as long as you like. Do not sell the name of the building itself, and never sell a name that already belongs to somebody, because the second time you sell it you are not selling space, you are erasing a person.

title: Before You Have Work Done on Your Flat
intro: Tadilat yaptıracaklara yönelik bir rehber okuyacaksın: teklifler nasıl okunur, ödeme nasıl bölünür, ne yazıya geçirilir.
text:
BEFORE YOU HAVE WORK DONE ON YOUR FLAT

Most disputes about building work do not start with bad work. They start with two people who each believed something different and never wrote it down.

Get three quotes, and read them side by side before you read the prices. A quote that is fifteen per cent cheaper is often cheaper because something has been left out: the removal of the old material, the disposal fee, the second coat. It is said in the trade that the second page is where the money is, and the second page is the one people skip.

Have the start and the end written into the contract, together with what happens if they move. It is widely reported that most delays are caused by materials, not by workers, and materials are ordered by whoever placed the order first. If you sign in March for work in September, ask when the order will actually be placed.

Do not have everything paid before the work is finished. A third at the start, a third in the middle and a third on completion is normal; anything above half in advance should be questioned. If you are asked for cash, ask for the reason in writing.

Photograph the room before anybody starts. It costs nothing and it settles nine arguments out of ten.

Finally, the point that is most often forgotten: agree who cleans. It sounds small until a Friday evening when you have your kitchen back but cannot cook in it. Have that written down as well. A sentence in a contract is cheaper than a phone call at nine on a Friday.

write things down before the work starts

questions.explain: „… often cheaper because something has been left out: the removal of the old material, the disposal fee, the second coat.“

title: Where Stolen Bikes Go
intro: Bisiklet hırsızlığı üzerine kısa bir sunum dinleyeceksin: yaygın inanışlar, gerçek rakamlar ve tek bir öneri.

segments.text: Good evening. I have twenty minutes and one message: almost everything you have been told about bicycle theft is a little bit wrong.
It is often said that bikes are stolen by organized gangs and driven abroad. Some are. But in this city, seventy per cent of recovered bikes are found within four kilometers of where they were taken.
It is also believed that expensive locks are the answer. They help, but the strongest lock in the world is useless around a wheel.
Now the part that matters. Every year we recover about eleven hundred bikes. Fewer than one in ten is returned to its owner.
That is not because we do not try. It is because we cannot prove whose bike it is.
A bike has a frame number, usually under the pedals. Almost nobody has ever written it down.
So here is what I would like you to do tonight. Turn the bike over, photograph the number, and send the photo to yourself.
If you buy a second-hand bike, have the number checked before you pay. It takes ten seconds on our website.
And if your bike is taken, report it with that number the same day. A bike that is reported without a number is reported to nowhere.
One last thing. If you find that a bike you own is on our list, do not be afraid to come. Nobody is assumed to be a thief for asking.
